summary.headline: Arvind acquires 61% of Dalco-GFT (via AAML) at 7.75x CY25 EBITDA; transaction valued at $136M EV.
summary.overview: Arvind Limited announced the acquisition of a 61% economic stake in Dalco-GFT, a US needle-punch nonwovens maker, through its subsidiary Arvind Advanced Materials Limited (AAML), at 7.75x CY2025 reported EBITDA. Management said the deal is EPS and margin accretive at consolidated level and that financing has closed. The call was restricted to the transaction because FY26 results were yet to be announced, so no FY26 financials were discussed. Management guided to Dalco-GFT growing mid-teens on a $5M-per-year capex run rate, versus about 10% historically. Full target financials and goodwill figures were deferred to Q1 FY27, with headline balance sheet numbers promised separately.

financial_highlights.value: 61% (about 70% economic interest per Mayank Tiwari's bridge)
About 60 days, in line with Arvind
$50 million total (up from $15 million; $35 million added)

financial_highlights.metric: Debt raised at Arvind India level

segments.name: Dalco-GFT (target, US needle-punch nonwovens)
segments.commentary: Established 1988, two US plants (South Carolina and North Carolina), 75 million lb capacity, about 85% utilised. Serves automotive (noise and vibration, largest segment) and geotextiles, roofing and flooring; about 75 customers and 88% of automotive platforms sole-sourced.

guidance_outlook: Management targets mid-teens revenue growth for Dalco-GFT, versus about 10% historically; Mayank Tiwari also cited 10-12% revenue growth and mid-teens margin growth as the business plan.
Indian business guidance of 18-20% growth is reiterated; the US entity is expected to grow slightly slower but still high teens.
Capex of about $5M per year (roughly one new line each year), with a capex plan for the current year to be ready in 3-4 months; about 3 more lines can fit in existing space.
Debt-reduction goal: wind down AAML acquisition debt over the next couple of years; financial ratios are within covenants and expected to improve within 12 months.
Full consolidation of Dalco-GFT from roughly two months into Q1 FY27; full Dalco-GFT financial statements to be shared with Q1 FY27 results.
Management expects to retain the existing top team; residual equity to be bought in tranches at 2 and 4 years.
capex_capacity: Dalco-GFT capacity of 75 million lb with about 85% utilisation; management says capacity is not a constraint for mid-teens growth.
Six lines in place, with four having been upgraded; three more lines can be accommodated in existing space at the two US facilities.
Gross block of Dalco-GFT stated at around $25 million (to be confirmed).
Capex run rate of about $5M per year, equal to one new line of capacity (about $4.5-5M each).
Manufacturing to stay near the point of consumption; no plan yet for a third US location (Texas or Mexico considered later).
demand_pricing: Management cites a TAM of about $2.5 billion across segments. Automotive (largest segment) grows 3-4%; noise and vibration reduction, the main product category, grows 6-7%.
Geotextile demand is expected to rise with US infrastructure spending, and roofing and flooring are also cited as growth areas.
Customer contracts are about 50% share with 5-6 year lives; 88% of products are sole-sourced and a model life is 6-7 years.

Raw materials are mostly polymers (polyester/polypropylene staple fibre), with 65-70% sourced in the US and the rest from Korea and Vietnam; polymer prices have risen with petroleum, with some pass-through so far.
No material seasonality; production per day is steady at 85% utilisation, with growth from capacity additions and pushing utilisation above 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation, and does capex need to rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 85%. Planned capex of about $5M per year is to be funded from internal accruals, with surplus cash used to pay down debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why do sellers exit now and how is management retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has rolled over a large part of its equity and holds about 39% in total; the founder holds about 16-17% for the 4-year period. Performance-linked long-term incentives were redone, and the financial sponsor is the main seller.

qa_highlights.question: How is the $136M EV funded given the $110M debt raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The EV of about $136M, plus about $16-17M net debt, implies about $84-85M of outlay for the stake. Sellers roll about $35-36M of equity into AAML, which explains the 61% stake and the debt split.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Dalco growing at only 10% historically?
qa_highlights.answer: The PE owners focused on efficiency and profitability (high-teen EBITDA margins) rather than capacity and new business development; the new plan lifts capex to about $5M per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk in the US expansion and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans a low-touch model with no change to the operating team; it says the workforce is under 150 with 70-80 blue-collar staff. Products are said to be broadly fungible across 3-4 end markets, and automotive is protected in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation and supplier/customer bargaining power?
qa_highlights.answer: The only inflation is in polymer raw materials, which are petroleum-linked; some cost increases have been passed on and management sees no derailment risk. Sole sourcing reflects deep specification into vehicle platforms.

risks_watch: Leverage: AAML debt rose to $50M and the US debt cost is about 5.5% SOFR-linked; covenant headroom depends on deleveraging over the next 12-24 months.
Full Dalco-GFT financials, goodwill and balance sheet figures were not disclosed on the call and remain outstanding until Q1 FY27 or the promised headline numbers.
Growth ramp: mid-teens growth depends on new lines and geotextile share gains, versus about 10% historically.
Polymer cost inflation linked to petroleum prices, if the war situation persists.
Cross-border integration and synergy execution (India manufacturing of nonwovens is only at an early stage, about 2.5 years out).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on strategic fit, growth and team quality, but evasive or deferred on numbers such as goodwill, full financials and India synergy details, which were pushed to later disclosures. Management stressed the call was restricted to the deal because FY26 results were pending.
key_quotes: So what this acquisition does is it gives us immediate scale and a very large addressable market in a technology that we understand very well.
I think the right question to ask is not why, but how we are managing that risk, and we are managing the risk because in multiple ways.
So I think it's a fair value.

adds.what: New needle-punch line at Dalco-GFT (about $5M/yr capex, roughly one line per year; current-year line ready in 3-4 months)
Up to 3 more lines can fit in existing space at Dalco-GFT's two US plants

growth.why: Management guides Indian business to high-teens growth (hopefully 20%+) and Dalco-GFT to mid-teens (vs ~10% historically), backed by ~$5M/yr capex for roughly one new line a year, 85% utilisation with room for ~3 more lines, and 88% sole-sourced auto platforms; order-level contracts and line-level numbers are only partly quantified.
